For crops, shade buffers severe temperature effects on understorey crops and lowers ambient temperature by 4°C, and in Kenya shade trees are described as buffering temperature fluctuations [ev_microclimate_buffering_dobhal24_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_watts22_1, ev_t3_microclimate_shade_quandt17_3, ev_microclimate_buffering_ipccar6_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_vannoordwijk21_1].

Only the Brazilian and Kenyan units are recorded as mixed crop-livestock; the others carry no or a different farming system and are applied by default [ev_microclimate_buffering_santos25_10, ev_t3_microclimate_shade_quandt17_3, ev_microclimate_buffering_dobhal24_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_ipccar6_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_moran18_3, ev_microclimate_buffering_moran18_8, ev_microclimate_buffering_vannoordwijk21_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_watts22_1]. The Ghanaian cocoa shade came from artificial shade nets rather than shade trees, so it captures above-ground shading only and its transfer to agroforestry is borderline [ev_microclimate_buffering_mensah23_1]. Recorded countries are Cuba (upper-middle income) and Ghana (lower-middle income); the other units have no country or income group, so the transfer is classed adjacent, and all the review units rest on temperature buffering, a component of heat-stress impact [ev_microclimate_buffering_moran18_3, ev_microclimate_buffering_mensah23_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_dobhal24_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_watts22_1].
